source.title: Purity for flat cohomology
source.version: arXiv 1912.10932v3 (26 April 2023, 'final version, to appear in Annals of Mathematics'), read in full in its TeX source and PDF. The published PDF is behind the Annals subscription and was not read. The authors' 27 February 2023 revision, the date the Annals page gives as 'Revised', was compared with v3 word by word: it differs in some section titles and small wordings, and two of the recorded misprints (E4, E8) occur only in v3. Locators give arXiv v3 numbering and pages; the numbering agrees with the February revision.
readSections: §1 Absolute cohomological purity for flat cohomology

baseline.note: Library items cite declarations read at the pinned commits: Mathlib's regular sequences, regular local rings, PreTilt and WittVector.fontaineTheta, Henselian pairs, localCohomology, CommRing.Pic, Azumaya algebras, ultrafilters and the Stone–Čech compactification, fppfTopology; Tau Ceti's Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes. Neither library has flat or étale cohomology of schemes, perfectoid rings as such, animated rings, Dieudonné theory or the arc-topology.

items.name: Regular sequences (EGA convention)
items.statement: Elements f_1, …, f_n of a ring A form a regular sequence on an A-module M if each f_i is a nonzerodivisor on M/(f_1, …, f_{i−1})M; following EGA 0_IV 15.1.7 there is no requirement that M/(f_1, …, f_n)M be nonzero. Consequences used throughout: for a regular sequence f_1, …, f_n, the sequence f_1^{e_1}, …, f_n^{e_n} with e_i ≥ 1 (and f_i^{1/n_i} when these roots exist) is again regular (Stacks 07DV), and in a Noetherian local ring every permutation of a regular sequence in the maximal ideal is regular.
items.note: Library: Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean:135 (IsWeaklyRegular, the EGA convention without the nonvanishing condition), :146 (IsRegular, which adds it) and :645 (permutations). The power and root stability (Stacks 07DV) is not in Mathlib; it is elementary and is part of the complete-intersection layer at R03.3.

items.name: Regular and unramified regular local rings
items.statement: A Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) is regular if 𝔪 is generated by dim(R) elements; it is unramified if it is of mixed characteristic (0, p) and p ∉ 𝔪².
items.note: Library: Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean:51. Unramifiedness is a one-line predicate on top of the library class.

items.name: Complete intersection local rings
items.statement: A Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) is a complete intersection if its 𝔪-adic completion R̂ is isomorphic to R̃/(f_1, …, f_n) for a complete regular local ring R̃ and an R̃-regular sequence f_1, …, f_n (R̃ may be chosen unramified when char(R/𝔪) = p > 0). Every ideal that cuts out a complete intersection in a regular local ring is generated by a regular sequence (Stacks 09Q1).
items.note: R03.3 plans regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings and the complete-intersection criteria for complete local rings; the definition through the completion and a Cohen presentation is the form used here.

items.name: Cohen structure theorem
items.statement: The completion of a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) is a quotient of a complete regular local ring R̃, which may be chosen unramified when char(R/𝔪) = p > 0. A complete regular local ring with residue field k is k⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧ in equal characteristic, and W(k)⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧/(p − f) with f = x_1 (unramified case) or f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_d)² when k is perfect of characteristic p.
items.locator: Section 1.4, p. 8; Lemma 3.1.1(b), p. 29; proof of Theorem 3.1.3, p. 30
items.note: Cited from EGA 0_IV 19.8.8(i) and Matsumura 29.7. Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing and power series rings but no Cohen structure theorem.

items.name: The Bégueri resolution
items.statement: For a commutative, finite, locally free group G over a scheme S with Cartier dual G^*, there is a short exact sequence 0 → G → Res_{G^*/S}(𝔾_m) → Q → 0 of fppf sheaves with Res_{G^*/S}(𝔾_m) and Q commutative, smooth, affine S-group schemes; the map Res_{G^*/S}(𝔾_m) → Q is faithfully flat and finitely presented, so the sequence stays exact on the fppf site of any animated algebra over S.
items.locator: Section 1.4, p. 8; equation (1.4.2); proof of Theorem 5.2.6, p. 56
items.note: Library: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineGroupScheme/CartierDuality/FiniteLocallyFree.lean:275 and :320 supply the Cartier dual. Cited from Bégueri, Mém. SMF 4 (1980), proposition 2.2.1, and Stacks 01ZT. The Cartier dual is in Tau Ceti; the Weil restriction and the resolution are not.

items.name: Descent and hyperdescent of 𝒟(ℤ)-valued functors; cardinal bounds for large sites
items.statement: A functor F on a subcategory of rings with values in 𝒟(ℤ) satisfies descent (resp. hyperdescent) for a topology T if F(A) ≅ R lim_Δ F(A'^•) for every T-cover A → A' with Čech nerve A'^• (resp. every T-hypercover A → A'^•). Large sites such as the fpqc site are cut down by a strong limit cardinal κ of uncountable cofinality, and every assertion is checked to be independent of κ. Descent implies hyperdescent for functors that are bounded below.
items.note: E2 plans Postnikov completion and unbounded cohomological descent; SF.1 plans fpqc and fppf descent.

items.name: The tilt, A_inf and Fontaine's θ
items.statement: For a ring A, the tilt is A^♭ = lim_{a ↦ a^p} A/pA. For p-adically complete A, the reduction map lim_{a ↦ a^p} A → lim_{a ↦ a^p} A/pA is a multiplicative bijection, giving a ↦ a^♯; tilting is right adjoint to W(−) between perfect 𝔽_p-algebras and p-adically complete ℤ_p-algebras; A_inf(A) = W(A^♭) with counit θ: A_inf(A) → A, θ([a]) = a^♯; θ is surjective iff A/pA is semiperfect; the functors (−)^♭, W(−) and A_inf(−) commute with limits. If A is ϖ-adically complete with ϖ | p, then A^♭ = lim_{a ↦ a^p} A/ϖA.
items.note: Library: Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634 (PreTilt A p = Perfection (ModP A p) p), Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt.lean:49, Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165, :182, :195. Mathlib has the tilt of any p-adically complete ring, θ and its surjectivity criterion. The W ⊣ (−)^♭ adjunction and the ϖ-variant are among Q0's A_inf/θ descriptions.

items.name: Integral perfectoid rings
items.statement: A ring A is perfectoid if (i) there is ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p such that A is ϖ-adically complete, and (ii) θ: A_inf(A) → A is surjective with principal kernel (BMS18 Definition 3.5). Equivalently, A ≅ W(B)/(ξ) for a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra B and ξ = (ξ_0, ξ_1, …) with B ξ_0-adically complete and ξ_1 ∈ B^× (then B ≅ A^♭ and ξ is a nonzerodivisor generating ker θ). An 𝔽_p-algebra is perfectoid iff it is perfect. Recognition: if A is ϖ-adically complete for a nonzerodivisor ϖ with ϖ^p | p and a ↦ a^p induces A/ϖ ≅ A/ϖ^p, then A is perfectoid.
items.note: Q0 constructs integral perfectoid rings in the scope of BS22 with their A_inf/θ descriptions; PR.0 proves the equivalence between perfect prisms and perfectoid rings (BS22 Theorem 3.10).

items.name: Basic identities of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For a perfectoid A that is ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p: there are ϖ^♭, p^♭ ∈ A^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯, (p^♭)^♯ unit multiples of ϖ and p, and a ↦ a^♯ induces A^♭/(ϖ^♭)^p ≅ A/ϖ^p and A^♭/p^♭ ≅ A/p; the p-power map A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p is bijective; A^♭⟨ϖ^♭⟩ ≅ A⟨ϖ⟩ as A_inf(A)-modules, so A^♭ is ϖ^♭-torsion free iff A is ϖ-torsion free; and A⟨ϖ^{1/p^∞}⟩ = A⟨ϖ⟩ = A⟨ϖ^∞⟩.

items.name: Canonical decomposition of a perfectoid ring; perfectoid rings are reduced
items.statement: For a perfectoid A that is ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p and Ā = A/A⟨ϖ^∞⟩, the ring Ā is a ϖ-torsion free perfectoid with tilt the analogous quotient of A^♭, and A ≅ Ā ×_{(Ā/ϖ)^red} (A/ϖ)^red, compatibly with A^♭ ≅ Ā^♭ ×_{(Ā/ϖ)^red} (A/ϖ)^red; moreover A/(ϖ^{1/p^∞}) ≅ (A/ϖ)^red is a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra. Every perfectoid ring is reduced, and if a ∈ A has compatible p-power roots then A⟨a^{1/p^n}⟩ = A⟨a⟩ = A⟨a^∞⟩.

items.name: Fibre products of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For a surjection f: A ↠ A' of perfectoid ℤ_p-algebras, A_inf(f) is surjective and induces surjections A_inf(A) ↠ A_inf(A') ×_{A'} A and [p^♭]A_inf(A) ↠ [p^♭]A_inf(A') ×_{pA'} pA (so a surjection on kernels of θ). For any map B → A' with B perfectoid, C = A ×_{A'} B is perfectoid with C^♭ ≅ A^♭ ×_{A'^♭} B^♭. In particular (Example 2.1.5), for a perfectoid A that is ϖ-adically complete with ϖ | p and a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra B over (A/ϖ)^red, A ×_{(A/ϖ)^red} B is perfectoid.

items.name: Completed ind-étale algebras over a perfectoid are perfectoid
items.statement: For a perfectoid A that is ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p, the ϖ-adic (for instance the p-adic) completion of every ind-étale A-algebra is perfectoid.
items.note: The Anschütz–Le Bras extraction records the same statement (its item 13) in its proposed prismatic Dieudonné Part II; one home should be chosen.

items.name: p-integral closedness of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For A ⊂ A', A is p-integrally closed in A' if a' ∈ A' with a'^p ∈ A lies in A; the p-integral closure is the smallest such subring containing A. For a nonzerodivisor ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p, the map A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p, a ↦ a^p, is injective iff A is p-integrally closed in A[1/ϖ]. Consequently, for a perfectoid A that is ϖ-adically complete, the image Ā ⊂ A[1/ϖ] is p-integrally closed and lim_{a ↦ a^p} A[1/ϖ] ≅ A^♭[1/ϖ^♭] compatibly with lim_{a ↦ a^p} A ≅ A^♭.

items.name: Perfectoid completions of p-integral closures
items.statement: Let ϖ ∈ A be a nonzerodivisor with ϖ^p | p having compatible p-power roots, such that a ↦ a^p is surjective from A/ϖ to A/ϖ^p. Then the ϖ-adic completion of the p-integral closure of A in A[1/ϖ] is perfectoid (a variant of Gabber–Ramero, Corollary 16.9.15).

items.name: The tilting equivalence for perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For a perfectoid ring A and a generator ξ = (ξ_0, ξ_1, …) of ker(θ: W(A^♭) → A), the functors A' ↦ A'^♭ and B ↦ W(B)/(ξ) are inverse equivalences between perfectoid A-algebras and ξ_0-adically complete perfect A^♭-algebras; A'^♭ is ϖ^♭-adically complete (for ϖ^♭ | ξ_0) iff A' is ϖ-adically complete for ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯.
items.note: PR.0 plans the equivalence between perfect prisms and perfectoid rings, of which this is the relative form; the completeness transfer is part of the same package.

items.name: Tilting perfectoid valuation rings
items.statement: In the tilting equivalence, A' is a valuation ring (resp. one with algebraically closed fraction field) iff A'^♭ is, and then x ↦ x^♯ identifies the value groups Frac(A'^♭)^×/(A'^♭)^× ≅ Frac(A')^×/(A')^×. Every localization of a perfectoid valuation ring, other than the zero-dimensional one in mixed characteristic, is again a perfectoid valuation ring (Remark 2.1.10).
items.locator: Proposition 2.1.9, p. 14; second part, p. 15; Remark 2.1.10, p. 15
items.note: Library: Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/ValuationRing.lean:64. Uses Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Theorem 3.7(ii) for rank ≤ 1, planned at PerfectoidSpaces P1.

items.name: Adjoining p-power roots, completed tensor products and products
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid ring, ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p. (a) The ϖ-adic completion of A[X_i^{1/p^∞}]_{i∈I} is perfectoid with tilt the ϖ^♭-adic completion of A^♭[(X_i^♭)^{1/p^∞}]. (b) For ϖ-adically complete perfectoid A-algebras A_i, the ϖ-adically completed tensor product ⊗̂_{i∈I} A_i is perfectoid with tilt ⊗̂ A_i^♭. (d) A product ∏ B_i of ℤ_p-algebras is perfectoid iff each B_i is, and (∏ B_i)^♭ ≅ ∏ B_i^♭.

items.name: Quotients of perfectoid rings by ideals with p-power roots
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid ring, ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p, and S ⊂ A a subset such that (S mod ϖ^n) is generated by p^n-th powers of its elements for all n > 0 (for instance, each s ∈ S has a root s^{1/p^N} ∈ S with N > 0). Then the ϖ-adic completion of A/(S) is perfectoid with tilt the ϖ^♭-adic completion of A^♭/(S^♭), S^♭ = lim_{a ↦ a^p}(S mod ϖ).

items.name: Adic completions of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For a perfectoid A, a_1^♭, …, a_r^♭ ∈ A^♭ and a_j = (a_j^♭)^♯, the (a_1, …, a_r)-adic completion of A is perfectoid, agrees with the derived (a_1, …, a_r)-adic completion, and has tilt the (a_1^♭, …, a_r^♭)-adic completion of A^♭.

items.name: Perfectoid rings are quotients of torsion-free perfectoid rings
items.statement: Every perfectoid A that is ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p is a quotient of a perfectoid Ã that is ϖ̃-torsion free and ϖ̃-adically complete for a lift ϖ̃ of ϖ with ϖ̃^p | p; every perfectoid ring is a quotient of a p-torsion free perfectoid ring.

items.name: Arc covers and I-complete arc covers
items.statement: A ring map A → A' is an arc cover if every A → V with V a valuation ring of rank ≤ 1 extends, after a faithfully flat extension V → V' of rank ≤ 1 valuation rings, along A → A'; for a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ A, it is an I-complete arc cover if this holds for the I-adically complete such V. One may restrict to V' (and V) that are I-adically complete with algebraically closed fraction fields, and the rank condition may be dropped. These covers define the arc and I-complete arc topologies; an I-complete arc cover is I'-complete for I ⊂ I', and reduces to an arc cover modulo I.

items.name: Examples of arc and I-complete arc covers
items.statement: (a) Every faithfully flat map is an arc cover. (b) Every map that is faithfully flat modulo the powers of a finitely generated ideal I is an I-complete arc cover. (c) Every integral map that is surjective on spectra is an arc cover.

items.name: Tilting preserves ϖ-complete arc covers
items.statement: For a map A → A' of perfectoid rings that are ϖ-adically complete (ϖ^p | p) and ϖ^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ, A → A' is a ϖ-complete arc cover iff A^♭ → A'^♭ is a ϖ^♭-complete arc cover.

items.name: Products of valuation rings form a base of the arc topology
items.statement: Every ring A (resp. with ϖ ∈ A) has an arc (resp. ϖ-complete arc) cover A → ∏_{i∈I} V_i by valuation rings (resp. ϖ-adically complete valuation rings) of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction fields.

items.name: Connected components of a product of valuation rings
items.statement: For valuation rings {V_i}_{i∈I}, the connected components of Spec(∏ V_i) are the Spec(∏_𝒰 V_i) for ultrafilters 𝒰 on I, via a continuous map Spec(∏ V_i) → βI to the Stone–Čech compactification. If all Frac(V_i) are algebraically closed, every quasi-compact open of Spec(∏ V_i) has no nonsplit étale covers and its connected components are spectra of valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields.
items.note: Library: Mathlib/Order/Filter/Ultrafilter/Defs.lean:41 and Mathlib/Topology/Compactification/StoneCech.lean:323.

items.name: Arc hyperdescent for étale cohomology (Bhatt–Mathew)
items.statement: For a ring A (resp. with finitely generated I ⊂ A) and a torsion sheaf F on A_ét, the functor A' ↦ RΓ_ét(A', F) satisfies arc hyperdescent on A-algebras, the functor A' ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec(Â') ∖ V(I), F) (I-adic completion) satisfies I-complete arc hyperdescent, and so does A' ↦ RΓ_ét(A'^h, F) for the I-Henselization.
items.note: Cited from Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 5.4, Mathew Remark 5.18 and Bhatt–Mathew Corollary 6.17; the I-complete version is deduced from their arc_I variant.

items.name: Henselization and completion agree on punctured étale cohomology
items.statement: For an ideal I ⊂ A' and a torsion sheaf F, RΓ_ét(Spec(A'^h) ∖ V(I), F) ≅ RΓ_ét(Spec(Â') ∖ V(I), F), where A'^h is the I-Henselization and Â' the I-adic completion; hence A' ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec(A'^h) ∖ V(I), F) satisfies I-complete arc hyperdescent.
items.note: Cited from Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 6.11 (the Fujiwara–Gabber theorem) and ILO14 XX 4.4.

items.name: Arc descent gives formal glueing
items.statement: A functor satisfying (I-complete) arc descent satisfies formal glueing: for a map A → A' inducing A/I^n ≅ A'/I^n, the square with vertices F(A), F(A'), F(A[1/f]) and F(A'[1/f]) (f ∈ I) is Cartesian.
items.locator: Theorem 2.2.7, p. 21; proof, p. 21; proof of Lemma 5.4.2, p. 65
items.note: Cited from Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 6.4.

items.name: Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change
items.statement: For a Henselian pair (A', I) and a torsion sheaf F on A'_ét, RΓ_ét(A', F) ≅ RΓ_ét(A'/IA', F).
items.locator: Theorem 2.2.5, p. 20; proof, p. 20; proof of Theorem 5.5.1, p. 68
items.note: Cited from Gabber, Israel J. Math. 87 (1994), Theorem 1. The Bhatt–Mathew extraction already routes this theorem to ArcTopologyAndDescent (its item 25).

items.name: Algebraic tilting of idempotents and étale cohomology
items.statement: Let A be ϖ-Henselian (ϖ^p | p) with bounded ϖ^∞-torsion and perfectoid ϖ-adic completion, and let Spec(A[1/ϖ]) ⊂ U ⊂ Spec(A) and Spec(A^♭[1/ϖ^♭]) ⊂ U^♭ ⊂ Spec(A^♭) be opens with complements identified via A^♭/ϖ^♭ ≅ A/ϖ. Then Idem(U) ≅ Idem(U^♭) compatibly with orthogonality and RΓ_ét(U, G) ≅ RΓ_ét(U^♭, G) for every torsion abelian group G, functorially in A, U and G; in particular RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(A^♭, G) for closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/ϖA).
items.note: The proof avoids adic spaces and almost purity: idempotents are handled by the multiplicative identifications of 2.1.1 and 2.1.7 with Beauville–Laszlo glueing, étale cohomology by I-complete arc descent (Theorem 2.2.5) reducing to products of valuation rings (Lemma 2.2.4).

items.name: The integral approximation lemma
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid ring, ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p, a ∈ A and m ≥ 0. There is a' ∈ A^♭ such that for every continuous valuation |·| on A with |A| ≤ 1, |a − a'^♯| ≤ |p|·max(|a'^♯|, |ϖ|^{pm}); in particular |a| ≤ |ϖ^{pm}| iff |a'^♯| ≤ |ϖ^{pm}|.
items.note: An integral variant of Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Corollary 6.7(i); compare Kedlaya–Liu 3.6.7.

items.name: Topological nilpotence detected by continuous valuations
items.statement: For a ring A with the ϖ-adic topology (ϖ a nonzerodivisor), a ∈ A[1/ϖ] is topologically nilpotent (a^n ∈ ϖA for large n) iff |a| < 1 for every continuous valuation |·| on A[1/ϖ] with |A| ≤ 1.
items.note: A special case of Gabber–Ramero, Corollary 15.4.27(ii); the proof uses Huber, Continuous valuations, Lemma 3.3(i).

items.name: Syntomic, ind-fppf and ind-syntomic ring maps
items.statement: A ring map A → A' is syntomic if Spec(A') is covered by spectra of A-algebras A[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) with each A[x]/(f_1, …, f_i) flat over A and f_1, …, f_c regular in A[x]_𝔭 for primes 𝔭 ⊇ (f); it is ind-fppf (resp. ind-syntomic) if A' is a filtered colimit of faithfully flat, finitely presented (resp. syntomic) A-algebras, equivalently if every A-map B → A' from a finitely presented B factors through a faithfully flat finitely presented (resp. syntomic) A-algebra. These classes are stable under composition, base change, finite products and filtered colimits; A → Â for a Noetherian local Q-algebra with a nonreduced formal fibre is flat but not ind-fppf.
items.note: Library: Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Basic.lean:63 and Mathlib/RingTheory/FinitePresentation.lean:44.

items.name: The ind-syntomic André lemma
items.statement: Let ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p have compatible p-power roots, and suppose either A is a ϖ-adically complete perfectoid, or A is ϖ-Henselian with perfectoid ϖ-adic completion and ϖ a nonzerodivisor. There are a faithfully flat, ind-syntomic, ϖ-Henselian A-algebra A' with perfectoid ϖ-adic completion Â' and a ϖ-divisible ideal I' ⊂ A' with A'/I' faithfully flat over A such that every monic P ∈ A'[T] has a root α_P ∈ A'/I' with compatible p-power roots α_P^{1/p^n} ∈ A'/I' (hence in Â'). In particular Â' contains compatible p-power roots of every a ∈ A and Â'/ϖ is faithfully flat over A/ϖ (Remark 2.3.5, recovering André's lemma in the form of Bhatt, Theorem 1.5).
items.locator: Theorem 2.3.4, p. 25; Remark 2.3.5, p. 25; proof, 2.3.6, pp. 25–28
items.note: Follows the method of Gabber–Ramero Theorem 16.9.17, improving flatness to ind-syntomicity and dropping torsion freeness; the proof reduces to one monic P and describes the p-integral closure of A_0[P/ϖ^m] explicitly.

items.name: André's flatness lemma (Bhatt–Scholze form)
items.statement: Every perfectoid ring A has a p-completely faithfully flat map to a perfectoid ring in which every element of A has compatible p-power roots (and which is absolutely integrally closed); Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 7.14 and Remark 7.15 even give ind-syntomicity modulo powers of p.
items.locator: Section 2.3, p. 22; footnote to the proof of Theorem 6.2.3, p. 84
items.note: Q3 plans BS22 Theorem 7.14; the paper notes that this version, with the p-adic continuity formula, suffices for the main theorem.

items.name: Semiperfectoid covers of p-Zariski rings
items.statement: Every ring A with 1 + pA ⊂ A^× has a faithfully flat map A → A_∞ such that the p-adic completion of A_∞^red is perfectoid, A_∞ is a quotient of a p-torsion free, p-Henselian ring Ã_∞ with perfectoid p-adic completion, and every monic polynomial over Ã_∞ (hence over A_∞ and A_∞^red) has a root.

items.name: Perfectoid towers over complete regular local rings
items.statement: (a) A complete regular local ring (R, 𝔪) with residue field k has a filtered system of regular, local, finite, flat R-algebras (R_i, 𝔪R_i), unramified if R is, whose colimit is regular local with residue field k̄. (b) If R is of mixed characteristic (0, p) with k perfect, so R ≅ W(k)⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧/(p − f) with f = x_1 or f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_d)², then R_n = W(k)⟦x_1^{1/p^n}, …, x_d^{1/p^n}⟧/(p − f) are regular, local, finite, flat of p-power rank over R, and the p-adic completion of R_∞ = colim R_n = W(k)⟦x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f) is perfectoid.
items.note: Restates Česnavičius, Purity for the Brauer group, Lemmas 5.1 and 5.2; the ⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧ notation is the colimit of the finite levels without further completion (1.4.1).

items.name: Étale cohomology of Henselian rings and their completions
items.statement: If A is a-Henselian with bounded a^∞-torsion, Â its a-adic completion and Spec(A[1/a]) ⊂ U ⊂ Spec(A) open, then RΓ_ét(U, F) ≅ RΓ_ét(U_Â, F) for every torsion sheaf F on U_ét; hence RΓ_Z(A, F) ≅ RΓ_Z(Â, F) for closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/aA), and RΓ_I(R, F) ≅ RΓ_I(R̂, F) for a Noetherian ring R that is I-Henselian.
items.note: Cited from Bouthier–Česnavičius, Theorem 2.3.4 and Corollary 2.3.5(e); earlier Fujiwara, Corollary 6.6.4, and ILO14 XX 4.4.

items.name: Local-to-global spectral sequence for cohomology with supports
items.statement: For a scheme X, a closed Z ⊂ X and an abelian sheaf F (étale or fppf), there is a spectral sequence E_2^{ij} = H^i_ét(X, ℋ^j_Z(−, F)) ⇒ H^{i+j}_Z(X, F), where ℋ^j_Z is the étale sheafification of X' ↦ H^j_Z(X', F); cohomology with supports sits in the triangle RΓ_Z(X, F) → RΓ(X, F) → RΓ(X ∖ Z, F).
items.locator: Lemma 7.1.1, p. 86; used in the proofs of Theorems 3.1.3, 3.2.4, 7.1.2 and 7.2.8
items.note: EDC.0 constructs cohomology with support as the localization fibre; SF.2 owns the étale and fppf sites. The spectral sequence is SGA 4 V 6.4 and Bouthier–Česnavičius Lemma 2.3.2.

items.name: Trace for finite flat maps and Artin's purity in positive characteristic
items.statement: For a finite flat map of degree invertible on the coefficients, the trace splits pullback on étale cohomology with supports (SGA 4 XVII 6.3.13–6.3.15). For a field k and the Henselization R of 𝔸^d_k at the origin, H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < 2d and ℓ invertible in k (SGA 4 XVI 3.7).
items.locator: Section 3.1, p. 29; proof of Theorem 3.1.3, p. 30
items.note: EDC.2:trace-purity builds the finite flat trace and the smooth trace f^*Λ(d)[2d] ≅ f^!Λ; with EDC.1:adjoint this gives i^!Λ ≅ Λ(−d)[−2d] for the origin of 𝔸^d_k, and a limit argument passes to the Henselization.

items.name: Absolute cohomological purity (Gabber–Thomason)
items.statement: For a regular local ring (R, 𝔪) and a commutative, finite, étale R-group G whose order is invertible in R, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < 2 dim(R).
items.locator: Theorem 3.1.3, p. 30; announced as Theorem 1.1.2, p. 3
items.note: The third proof: reduce to strictly Henselian complete R and G = ℤ/ℓ (Lemma 3.1.2); equal characteristic is Artin's theorem; in mixed characteristic pass by finite flat traces to the perfectoid tower of Lemma 3.1.1 and tilt with Theorem 2.2.7 to k⟦x_1^♭, …, x_d^♭⟧. The known proofs are Gabber's in Fujiwara (2002) after Thomason, and ILO14 XVI.

items.name: Full absolute purity reduces to positive characteristic
items.statement: For n invertible in a regular local R, the étale sheafified cohomology with supports satisfies ℋ^i_𝔪(−, ℤ/n) = 0 for i ≠ 2 dim(R) and ℋ^{2 dim R}_𝔪(−, ℤ/n) ≅ ℤ/n(−dim R) via the cycle class map; the argument of Theorem 3.1.3 reduces this to positive characteristic (after an injectivity argument as in Fujiwara, Lemma 2.3.1).

items.name: Virtual dimension of a Noetherian local ring
items.statement: For a Noetherian local (R, 𝔪) with R̂ ≅ R̃/I, R̃ complete regular local, vdim(R) = dim(R̃) − μ(I), where μ(I) is the minimal number of generators of I; it does not depend on the presentation (SGA 2 XIV 5.2).

items.name: Properties of the virtual dimension
items.statement: vdim(R) ≤ dim(R) with equality iff R is a complete intersection (SGA 2 XIV 5.4); vdim(R) = vdim(R̂) = vdim(R^h); for a flat local map R → R' of Noetherian local rings, vdim(R') = vdim(R) + vdim(R'/𝔪R') (Avramov), so vdim(R) = vdim(R^sh).

items.name: Depth and virtual dimension are not comparable
items.statement: A Cohen–Macaulay R that is not a complete intersection has depth_𝔪(R) > vdim(R); conversely every regular local ring R̃ has a three-generated ideal I with depth_𝔪(R̃/I) = 0 and vdim(R̃/I) ≥ dim(R̃) − 3 (Burch, Kohn and Auslander–Buchsbaum).

items.name: Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem
items.statement: For a strictly Henselian, complete, regular local ring R, f ∈ 𝔪 and ℓ invertible in R, H^i(R[1/f], ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i > dim(R); this is a case of Gabber's affine Lefschetz theorem for strictly Henselian quasi-excellent local rings.
items.note: Cited from ILO14 XV Corollaire 1.2.4.

items.name: Dualizing complexes on regular local rings and local duality
items.statement: On a strictly Henselian excellent regular local R with ℓ invertible, (μ_ℓ^{⊗ dim R})[2 dim R] is a dualizing complex for torsion étale sheaves, normalized so that local duality holds, and its j^!-pullback along an open immersion j is dualizing; Rj_* ∘ D ≅ D ∘ j_!, and local duality identifies H^i_𝔪(R, j_!ℤ/ℓ) with the dual of the stalk of H^{−i}(RHom(j_!ℤ/ℓ, (μ_ℓ^{⊗d})[2d])).
items.note: Cited from ILO14 XVII Théorème 0.2 and XVI Théorème 3.1.1, SGA 4 XVIII 3.1.8(iii), SGA 5 I 1.12(a) and (4.2.2).

items.name: A Lefschetz hyperplane theorem in local étale cohomology
items.statement: For a regular local (R, 𝔪), f ∈ 𝔪 and a prime ℓ invertible in R, H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) → H^i_𝔪(R/(f), ℤ/ℓ) is bijective for i < dim(R) − 1 and injective for i = dim(R) − 1; equivalently H^i_𝔪(R, j_!ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < dim(R) with j: Spec(R[1/f]) ↪ Spec(R).

items.name: The étale depth is at least the virtual dimension (order invertible)
items.statement: For a Noetherian local (R, 𝔪) and a commutative, finite, étale R-group G of order invertible in R, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < vdim(R).
items.note: Theorem 3.1.3 and Lemma 3.2.3 give the hypersurface case; a Mayer–Vietoris sequence over R_1 = R̃/(f_1, …, f_{n−1}), R_2 = R̃/(f_n), R_12 = R̃/(f_1f_n, …, f_{n−1}f_n) lowers the number of equations. The reduction works for every finite étale G and is reused in Theorem 6.2.4.

items.name: Zariski–Nagata purity for regular rings
items.statement: For a regular Noetherian scheme X and a closed Z ⊂ X of codimension ≥ 2, pullback is an equivalence from finite étale X-schemes to finite étale (X ∖ Z)-schemes (SGA 2 X Théorème 3.4(i)).
items.locator: Section 3.3, p. 34; proof of Theorem 3.3.1(b), p. 35

items.name: Algebraization of formal sections and of coherent formal modules
items.statement: For a complete Noetherian local ring and the formal completion along an ideal of the punctured spectrum: under depth ≥ 2 (resp. ≥ 3) conditions, morphisms (resp. coherent modules) on the formal completion of the punctured spectrum algebraize to an open neighbourhood, uniquely up to shrinking (Stacks 0DXR with 0DX9, and 0EJP; Raynaud 1975, I.3.9).
items.locator: Section 3.3, p. 34; proof of Theorem 3.3.1, pp. 34–35
items.note: SF.4 plans formal schemes and algebraization with a comparison to the completion; these are its punctured-spectrum cases.

items.name: Zariski–Nagata purity for rings of virtual dimension ≥ 3
items.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be Noetherian local and U_R = Spec(R) ∖ {𝔪}. (a) If vdim(R) ≥ 2, then pullback from finite étale R-schemes to finite étale U_R-schemes is fully faithful, U_R is connected and π_1^ét(U_R) ↠ π_1^ét(R). (b) If vdim(R) ≥ 3, the pullback is an equivalence and π_1^ét(U_R) ≅ π_1^ét(R).
items.note: Generalizes SGA 2 X 3.4 (complete intersections of dimension ≥ 3) and Cutkosky; purely classical, from de Jong's algebraization results and Zariski–Nagata for regular rings.

items.name: Étale fundamental groups from Galois categories
items.statement: The finite étale site of a connected scheme is a Galois category, its fundamental group classifies finite étale covers, and full faithfulness or equivalence of a pullback of finite étale sites translates into surjectivity or bijectivity on π_1^ét (SGA 1 V 6.9, 6.10).
items.locator: Section 3.3, p. 34; proof of Theorem 3.3.1, p. 34

items.name: Crystalline Dieudonné theory over perfect bases (Berthelot, Gabber, Lau)
items.statement: For a perfect 𝔽_p-scheme S there is a covariant equivalence G ↦ 𝕄(G) from commutative, finite, locally free S-groups that are locally of p-power order to quasi-coherent W(𝒪_S)-modules 𝕄 with semilinear F and Frob^{−1}-semilinear V, FV = VF = p, whose sections over affines Spec(R) are finitely presented, killed by a power of p and of projective dimension ≤ 1 over W(R). Locally 𝕄(G) = coker(𝕄(H_0) ↪ 𝕄(H_1)) for 0 → G → H_0 → H_1 → 0 with H_i p-divisible, where 𝕄(H) is the value of the covariant Dieudonné crystal 𝔻(H) = ℰxt^1_cris(H^*, 𝒪) on {(S, W_n(𝒪_S))}; its formation commutes with base change along perfect S-schemes.
items.note: Gabber's unpublished theorem after Berthelot 1980 (théorème 3.4.1), reproved by Lau (JAMS 2013, Corollary 6.5); uses Berthelot–Breen–Messing. It is the perfect-base case of the perfectoid classification, with which the prismatic functor is identified (Anschütz–Le Bras 4.44, 5.4).

items.name: Dieudonné modules of ℤ/p^n and μ_{p^n} over perfect bases
items.statement: 𝕄(ℤ/p^n) is W(𝒪_S)/p^n with F = p·Frob and V = Frob^{−1}; 𝕄(μ_{p^n}) is W(𝒪_S)/p^n with F = Frob and V = p·Frob^{−1} (Berthelot–Breen–Messing, exemple 4.2.16(i)).

items.name: The crystalline Dieudonné functor is exact
items.statement: In 4.1.1, G ↦ 𝕄(G) and its inverse preserve short exact sequences.

items.name: Low-degree flat cohomology over perfect bases
items.statement: For a perfect 𝔽_p-scheme S and a commutative, finite, locally free S-group G killed by p^n, functorially in G on S_ét: G ≅ ℋom(ℤ/p^n, G) ≅ ℋom_{W_n(𝒪_S), F, V}(𝟙_n, 𝕄(G)) ≅ 𝕄(G)^{V=1} and ℰxt^1_S(ℤ/p^n, G) ≅ ℰxt^1_{W_n(𝒪_S), F, V}(𝟙_n, 𝕄(G)) ≅ 𝕄(G)/(V − 1)𝕄(G).

items.name: The pro-fppf site
items.statement: A scheme map X' → X is pro-ppf (resp. pro-fppf) if X' is covered by affine opens Spec(A') mapping to affine opens Spec(A) ⊂ X with A' a filtered colimit of flat, finitely presented A-algebras (resp. and X' → X faithfully flat); pro-ppf families form a pro-fppf cover if every quasi-compact open is a finite union of images of quasi-compact opens. Pro-fppf covers are fpqc covers.

items.name: Perfection preserves fpqc and pro-fppf covers
items.statement: For a perfect 𝔽_p-scheme S, if {X_i → S} is an fpqc (resp. pro-fppf) cover, so is {X_i^perf → S}.

items.name: The Artin–Schreier–Witt sequence for Dieudonné modules
items.statement: For a perfect 𝔽_p-scheme S and G commutative, finite, locally free, locally of p-power order, 0 → G → 𝕄(G) --(V−1)--> 𝕄(G) → 0 is exact on perfect S-schemes with the pro-fppf topology, functorially in G.

items.name: The key formula in positive characteristic
items.statement: For a perfect 𝔽_p-scheme S and G commutative, finite, locally free, locally of p-power order, ε: S_fppf → S_ét gives a functorial triangle Rε_*(G) → 𝕄(G) --(V−1)--> 𝕄(G) → Rε_*(G)[1] on S_ét. If G is killed by p^n, then for any closed Z ⊂ S, RΓ_Z(S, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(W_n(S), 𝕄(G))^{V=1}, functorially in S, Z and G.
items.note: A perfect-ring variant of Kato–Trihan, Proposition 5.10, proved on the pro-fppf site following Gabber's suggestion.

items.name: Flat cohomology of perfect rings vanishes in degrees ≥ 2
items.statement: For a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra A and G commutative, finite, locally free of p-power order, H^i(A, G) = 0 for i ≥ 2.

items.name: Local cohomology vanishes below the length of a regular sequence
items.statement: If a_1, …, a_d ∈ A is regular on an A-module M and vanishes on a closed Z ⊂ Spec(A), then H^i_Z(A, M) = 0 for i < d; for a Noetherian local (R, 𝔪), H^i_𝔪(R, 𝔾_a) = 0 for i < depth(R) (SGA 2 III 3.3(iv)). No Noetherian hypothesis is needed for the first statement.
items.locator: Example 4.1.10, p. 39; proofs of Proposition 4.1.13 and Theorem 6.1.2, pp. 40–41, 82
items.note: Library: Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/LocalCohomology.lean:175 (local cohomology of modules). R03.3 plans depth and regular sequences; the non-Noetherian decreasing induction along A/(a_0, …, a_j) used for A_inf(A) and W(R_∞) must be included there.

items.name: Depth bounds for α_p and ℤ/p in positive characteristic
items.statement: For a Noetherian local 𝔽_p-algebra (R, 𝔪), the Frobenius-kernel and Artin–Schreier sequences give H^i_𝔪(R, α_p) = 0 and H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/p) = 0 for i < depth(R); for complete intersections this is a case of the main theorem.

items.name: Killing roots of a regular sequence changes flat cohomology only in high degrees
items.statement: Let f_1, …, f_m ∈ A be a regular sequence and G a commutative (A/(f_1, …, f_m))-group scheme that is smooth or finite locally free. For n_i > 0 with f_i^{1/n_i} ∈ A and an ideal I ⊂ A/(f_1, …, f_m) containing an (A/(f_1, …, f_m))-regular sequence of length d, H^i_I(A/(f_1, …, f_m), G) → H^i_I(A/(f_1^{1/n_1}, …, f_m^{1/n_m}), G) is injective for i < d and bijective for i < d − 1.
items.note: This is where the complete intersection hypothesis enters: the square-zero ideals are free, so deformation theory (Bouthier–Česnavičius Lemma B.14) and depth control the difference.

items.name: Passing to a finite flat cover of complete intersections
items.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) → (R', 𝔪') be a finite, flat, local map of Noetherian local complete intersections, n < dim(R) and G a commutative, finite, flat R-group. If H^i_𝔮(A, G) = 0 for i < n for every local ring (A, 𝔮) at a maximal ideal of every finite nonempty tensor power R' ⊗_R ⋯ ⊗_R R', then H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < n and H^n_𝔪(R, G) ↪ H^n_{𝔪'}(R', G).

items.name: Purity for flat cohomology in positive characteristic
items.statement: For a complete, Noetherian, local 𝔽_p-algebra (R, 𝔪) that is a complete intersection with perfect residue field and a commutative, finite, flat R-group G of p-power order, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < dim(R).

items.name: Prismatic Dieudonné theory over perfectoid rings (Lau, Scholze–Weinstein, Anschütz–Le Bras)
items.statement: For a perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra A and a generator ξ of ker(A_inf(A) → A), G ↦ 𝕄(G) = Ext^1_{A_Δ}(G^*, 𝒪_Δ) is a covariant equivalence, compatible with base change, from commutative, finite, locally free A-groups of p-power order to finitely presented, p-power torsion A_inf(A)-modules of projective dimension ≤ 1 with semilinear F and Frob^{−1}-semilinear V, FV = Frob(ξ), VF = ξ. For perfect 𝔽_p-algebras it agrees with the crystalline functor of 4.1.1, and for the p^n-torsion of a p-divisible group 𝕄(G) is finite projective over A_inf(A)/p^n.
items.note: Cited from Anschütz–Le Bras Theorem 5.4 (building on Scholze–Weinstein Theorem 17.5.2 and Lau 2018), and Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.8 for the A_inf(A)-module structure.

items.name: Prismatic Dieudonné modules of μ_{p^n} and ℤ/p^n
items.statement: 𝕄(μ_{p^n}) is A_inf(A)/p^n with F = Frob and V = ξ·Frob^{−1}; 𝟙_n = 𝕄(ℤ/p^n) is A_inf(A)/p^n with F = Frob(ξ)·Frob and V = Frob^{−1} (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.75).

items.name: The prismatic Dieudonné functor is exact
items.statement: In 4.2.1, G ↦ 𝕄(G) and its inverse preserve short exact sequences (part of Anschütz–Le Bras Theorem 5.4, since Cartier duality is exact).

items.name: Low-degree flat cohomology of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For a perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra A and G commutative, finite, locally free of p-power order, functorially in A and G: G(A) ≅ 𝕄(G)^{V=1} and H^1(A, G) ≅ 𝕄(G)/(V − 1)𝕄(G); the higher H^{≥2}(A, G) vanish (Remark 4.2.5, proved in Corollary 5.3.7).

items.name: p-complete arc hyperdescent for A_inf, A and A^♭ on perfectoid rings
items.statement: The functors A ↦ A_inf(A), A ↦ A and A ↦ A^♭ satisfy hyperdescent for p-complete arc hypercovers whose terms are perfectoid ℤ_p-algebras.
items.note: Restates Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Proposition 8.10; the proof tilts (Lemma 2.2.2) and uses v-descent for S ↦ S_perf (Bhatt–Scholze 2017, Theorem 4.1(i) and Proposition 4.5) upgraded to arc descent by Bhatt–Mathew Proposition 4.8.

items.name: p-complete arc hyperdescent for Dieudonné-module cohomology
items.statement: For a perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra A, closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA), a ∈ A_inf(A) and G commutative, finite, locally free of p-power order, A' ↦ 𝕄(G_{A'})[1/a] and A' ↦ RΓ_Z(A_inf(A'), 𝕄(G_{A'})) satisfy hyperdescent for p-complete arc hypercovers whose terms are perfectoid A-algebras.

items.name: Finitely presented modules over a product of rings
items.statement: For rings {R_i}_{i∈I} and a finitely presented ∏ R_i-module M, M ≅ ∏_i (M ⊗_{∏ R_j} R_i).

items.name: Dieudonné modules over a product of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For perfectoid A_i, A = ∏ A_i (perfectoid) and G over A commutative, finite, locally free of p-power order, 𝕄(G) ≅ ∏ 𝕄(G_{A_i}) over A_inf(A) ≅ ∏ A_inf(A_i), compatibly with F and V for compatible choices of ξ.

items.name: Unit-root φ-modules over an algebraically closed field
items.statement: For an algebraically closed field K of characteristic p and a finite K-vector space M with bijective Frobenius-semilinear F, M^{F=1} is a finite 𝔽_p-space and M ≅ M^{F=1} ⊗_{𝔽_p} K compatibly with Frobenius.
items.locator: Proposition 4.2.10, p. 43; proof of Claim 4.2.10.1, p. 45
items.note: Cited from Katz, p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms, Proposition 4.1.1.

items.name: Flat cohomology and Dieudonné modules over products of valuation rings
items.statement: Let A = ∏ A_i for p-adically complete rank ≤ 1 valuation rings A_i with algebraically closed fraction fields, a ∈ A and G commutative, finite, locally free of p-power order. Then V − 1 is surjective on 𝕄(G)[1/[a^♭]] for any choice of ξ, H^j(A[1/a], G) = 0 for j ≥ 1, and there is a unique commutative square G(A) ≅ 𝕄(G)^{V=1} over G(A[1/a]) ≅ (𝕄(G)[1/[a^♭]])^{V=1} whose vertical maps are bijective when a is a nonzerodivisor.

items.name: Free generation by 1-sifted colimits
items.statement: For a category C with filtered (resp. 1-sifted) colimits, C^fp (resp. C^sfp) consists of the objects X for which Hom(X, −) commutes with filtered (resp. 1-sifted: filtered colimits and reflexive coequalizers) colimits, and C^fp ↪ Ind(C^fp) ↪ C, C^sfp ↪ sInd(C^sfp) ↪ C are fully faithful. If C is cocomplete and generated under colimits by C^sfp, then sInd(C^sfp) ≅ C, the finitely presented objects are the (reflexive) coequalizers of objects of C^sfp and Ind(C^fp) ≅ C (Proposition 5.1.2). For Set, groups, abelian groups and rings, C^sfp consists of the retracts of finite free objects (Example 5.1.3).
items.locator: Paragraph 5.1.1, p. 46; Proposition 5.1.2, p. 47; Example 5.1.3, p. 47
items.note: E5:presentability plans Ind-completion and compact objects, and E5:animation sifted left Kan extensions; the 1-categorical statements follow Adámek–Rosický–Vitale and HA 4.7.3.18.

items.name: Animation of a category; anima; animated rings and modules
items.statement: For C cocomplete and generated under colimits by C^sfp, Ani(C) is the ∞-category freely generated under sifted colimits by C^sfp; it is presentable, has truncations τ_{≤n} and contains C as its 0-truncated objects with π_0 left adjoint to the inclusion, and a 1-sifted-colimit-preserving F: C → D induces Ani(F). Ani(Set) is anima (spaces), Ani(Ab) ≅ 𝒟^{≤0}(ℤ), Ani(Ring) is simplicial commutative rings up to weak equivalence; for an animated ring A, A[1/a] = A ⊗^L_{ℤ[X]} ℤ[X^{±1}], A/^L(a_1, …, a_n) = A ⊗^L_{ℤ[X_1, …, X_n]} ℤ, π_*(A), Mod(A) and the animated modules Mod^{≤0}(A), with derived tensor products obtained by animation.
items.note: E5:animation constructs animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings by sifted left Kan extension; DD.1 plans derived Koszul quotients and completions.

items.name: Composing animated functors
items.statement: For 1-sifted-colimit-preserving F: C → D and G: D → E between cocomplete categories generated by their strongly finitely presented objects, there is a natural transformation Ani(G) ∘ Ani(F) → Ani(G ∘ F); it is an equivalence if F(C^sfp) ⊂ Ind(D^sfp) or Ani(G)(F(C^sfp)) ⊂ E. In particular the forgetful functors Ani(Ring) → Ani(Ab) → Ani compose well and commute with limits.

items.name: Cotangent complex and square-zero extensions of animated rings
items.statement: For an animated ring A and animated A-module M, A ⊕ M is defined by animation; derivations are sections of A ⊕ M → A; L_{A/ℤ} corepresents them, agrees with the classical cotangent complex for 0-truncated A, and for A' → A the relative L_{A/A'} is the cofibre of L_{A'/ℤ} ⊗^L A → L_{A/ℤ}, with transitivity triangle and base change L_{A/A'} ⊗^L_A B ≅ L_{B/B'}. A square-zero extension with ideal M is a pullback A' = A ×_{A ⊕ M[1]} A along a derivation s: A → A ⊕ M[1], equivalently a map L_{A/A'} → M[1].
items.note: DD.0 constructs L_{B/A} by simplicial resolutions and characterizes it by square-zero extensions and derived derivations, with transitivity and derived base change.

items.name: Examples of square-zero extensions of animated rings
items.statement: (a) A ⊕ M → A is a square-zero extension. (b) A square-zero extension A' ↠ A of ordinary rings with kernel M is one of animated rings, via τ_{≤1}(L_{A/A'}) ≅ M[1]. (c) For an (m + 1)-truncated animated A', τ_{≤m}(A') is a square-zero extension by π_{m+1}(A')[m + 1], via τ_{≤m+2}(L_{τ≤m A'/A'}) ≅ π_{m+1}(A')[m + 2] (SAG 25.3.6.1).

items.name: The deformation complex of a flat affine group scheme
items.statement: For a ring R and a commutative, flat, affine R-group G, G(A) is an animated abelian group for animated R-algebras A, and M ↦ Fib(G(A ⊕ M) → G(A)) is corepresented by L_{G_A/A}, whose underlying animated A-module is e^*(L_{G/R}) ⊗^L_R A, so it commutes with base change. If G is of finite presentation (resp. smooth), e^*(L_{G/R}) has perfect amplitude [−1, 0] (resp. [0, 0]) and trivial ℤ-module structure.
items.note: Uses Illusie, Complexe cotangent II, VII (3.1.1.3), and HTT 5.5.2.7 for corepresentability.

items.name: Deformation fibre sequence for group-valued points
items.statement: For a flat, affine, commutative R-group G of finite presentation with unit section e and a square-zero extension of animated R-algebras A' ↠ A with ideal M, there is a functorial fibre sequence of animated abelian groups G(A') → G(A) → Hom_R(e^*(L_{G/R}), M[1]); in 𝒟(ℤ) the last term is the connective cover of RHom.
items.note: The proof of the fibre sequence is credited to Lurie.

items.name: Flat, faithfully flat and étale maps of animated rings
items.statement: An animated A-module M is flat (resp. faithfully flat) if π_0(M) is so over π_0(A) and π_*(A) ⊗_{π_0 A} π_0(M) ≅ π_*(M); then π_*(M' ⊗^L_A M) ≅ π_*(M') ⊗_{π_0 A} π_0(M) for every animated M'. A map of animated rings is flat, faithfully flat, étale, finitely presented or finite if A' is flat and π_0(f) has the property; fpqc, fppf and étale covers define Grothendieck topologies on animated rings and give no new covers of 0-truncated rings.
items.note: Uses Quillen's Tor spectral sequence (Homotopical algebra II.6, Theorem 6(b)). The text has a misprint here (sourceIssues).

items.name: Flatness is insensitive to nilpotent thickenings
items.statement: If A → A' induces π_0(A) ↠ π_0(A') with nilpotent kernel, an animated A-module M is (faithfully) flat iff A' ⊗^L_A M is; in particular M ≃ 0 iff A' ⊗^L_A M ≃ 0.

items.name: The étale site of an animated ring
items.statement: For an animated ring A, π_0 (equivalently base change) is an equivalence from étale (resp. finite étale) A-algebras to étale (resp. finite étale) π_0(A)-algebras; L_{A'/A} ≃ 0 for étale A'.

items.name: Étale and fppf cohomology over an animated ring
items.statement: For an animated ring A, étale, fppf and fpqc sheaves (the last with a cardinal bound) are ∞-sheaves on flat A-algebras; RΓ_ét(A, F) and RΓ_fppf(A, F) are the values of sheafifications, and RΓ_fppf(U_A, F) = R lim RΓ_fppf(A', F) over fppf A' factoring through an open U ⊂ Spec(π_0 A). For 0-truncated A this is classical cohomology; for a commutative affine R-group G, G(A) ≅ τ^{≤0} RΓ_fppf(A, G), so cohomology may be nonzero in negative degrees; quasi-coherent sheaves are hypersheaves.

items.name: Grothendieck's comparison of fppf and étale cohomology for smooth groups
items.statement: For a scheme X and a smooth commutative group scheme G over X, H^i_ét(X, G) ≅ H^i_fppf(X, G); consequently, by the Bégueri resolution, R^{≥2}ε_*(G) = 0 for ε: X_fppf → X_ét and G finite locally free.
items.locator: Section 5.2, p. 53; proofs of Theorem 5.2.6, p. 56, and Corollary 5.3.7, p. 61
items.note: SF.2 owns the Zariski, étale, fppf and pro-étale site comparisons; Grothendieck, Le groupe de Brauer III, 11.7.

items.name: fppf hyperdescent and Postnikov convergence over animated rings
items.statement: For a ring R and an affine commutative R-group G that is smooth or finite locally free, A ↦ RΓ_fppf(A, G) satisfies fppf hyperdescent on animated R-algebras and RΓ_fppf(A, G) ≅ R lim_n RΓ_fppf(τ_{≤n} A, G); if G is smooth even A ↦ RΓ_ét(A, G) satisfies fppf hyperdescent and RΓ_ét(A, G) ≅ RΓ_fppf(A, G). More generally (Corollary 5.2.7), for a tower A_n of A-algebras with τ_{≤n}(A) ≅ τ_{≤n}(A_n), RΓ_fppf(A, G) ≅ R lim_n RΓ_fppf(A_n, G).

items.name: The deformation triangle for flat cohomology
items.statement: For G affine commutative over R, smooth or finite locally free, and a square-zero extension of animated R-algebras A' ↠ A with ideal M, there is a functorial fibre sequence RΓ_fppf(A', G) → RΓ_fppf(A, G) → RHom_R(e^*(L_{G/R}), M[1]) in 𝒟(ℤ).

items.name: Positive-degree cohomology sees only π_0; nil-invariance
items.statement: For G smooth (resp. finite locally free) affine commutative over R: H^i(A, G) → H^i(π_0 A, G) is surjective for all i and bijective for i ≥ 0 (resp. i ≥ 1) (Corollary 5.2.9); for an ideal I of nilpotent elements of R, H^i(R, G) → H^i(R/I, G) is surjective for i ≥ 0 (resp. i ≥ 1) and bijective for i ≥ 1 (resp. i ≥ 2) (Corollary 5.2.10).

items.name: Rings without nonsplit fppf covers
items.statement: Every ring R has an ind-fppf R-algebra R̃ with no nonsplit fppf covers, which may be chosen IR̃-Henselian for an ideal I contained in every maximal ideal; the same holds with ind-étale, ind-smooth or ind-syntomic in place of ind-fppf (Remark 5.3.2).

items.name: A derived Beauville–Laszlo lemma
items.statement: For a map A → A' of animated rings and a ∈ A with A/^L a ≅ A'/^L a, A ≅ A' ×_{A'[1/a]} A[1/a], even in 𝒟(ℤ).

items.name: π_0 of a derived completion
items.statement: For an animated ring A, a ∈ A and Â = R lim_n A/^L a^n, the ring π_0(Â) is a square-zero extension of the a-adic completion of π_0(A) by lim^1_n π_1(A/^L a^n).

items.name: The p-adic continuity formula for flat cohomology
items.statement: For a prime p, a ring R, a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G of p-power order and an animated R-algebra A with π_0(A) p-Henselian, RΓ_fppf(A, G) ≅ R lim_n RΓ_fppf(A/^L p^n, G).
items.locator: Theorem 5.3.5, p. 59; equation (5.3.5.1); Claim 5.3.5.3, p. 59; announced as Theorem 1.2.5, p. 7
items.note: A flat analogue of Gabber's affine proper base change, new even for p-adically complete p-torsion free rings. The proof reduces to 0-truncated A, descends along covers faithfully flat modulo p to rings without nonsplit fppf covers, and checks a Mittag-Leffler condition via the deformation sequence.

items.name: Cohomological dimension of flat cohomology of p-Henselian rings
items.statement: For G commutative, finite, locally free of p-power order over R and an animated R-algebra A with π_0(A) p-Henselian, H^i(A, G) = 0 for i ≥ 3, and for i ≥ 2 if (π_0(A)/p)^red is perfect; this extends Corollary 4.1.9 and, for G = μ_p over 𝔽_p-algebras, a theorem of Treger.

items.name: Passing to derived p-adic completions in flat cohomology
items.statement: For G of p-power order and a map A → A' of animated R-algebras with π_0(A), π_0(A') p-Henselian and A/^L p ≅ A'/^L p, RΓ(U_A, G) ≅ RΓ(U_{A'}, G) for every open Spec(π_0(A)[1/p]) ⊂ U ⊂ Spec(π_0 A), hence RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(A', G) for its complement Z.

items.name: Semiperfect algebras over a perfect ring agreeing modulo a
items.statement: For a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra A, a semiperfect A-algebra A' and a ∈ A with A/^L a ≅ A'/^L a, ker(A' ↠ A'_perf) is uniquely a-divisible and A'/^L a ≅ A'_perf/^L a.

items.name: Elementary excision for flat cohomology
items.statement: For a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G, a map A → A' of animated R-algebras and a ∈ A with A/^L a ≅ A'/^L a, RΓ_{a=0}(A, G) ≅ RΓ_{a=0}(A', G); equivalently the square RΓ(A, G) → RΓ(A[1/a], G) over RΓ(A', G) → RΓ(A'[1/a], G) is Cartesian.
items.note: Proved in five steps: reduce to 𝔽_p-algebras (p-Henselization, arc-descent formal glueing and p-adic continuity), to 0-truncated perfect A, to 0-truncated A', conclude for perfect A and A' by Theorem 4.1.8 and the derived Beauville–Laszlo lemma, and remove perfectness of A' with Lemma 5.4.1.

items.name: The excision condition
items.statement: For a map f: A → A' of animated rings and I = (a_1, …, a_r) ⊂ π_0(A): π_0(A)/I ≅ (π_0(A)/I) ⊗^L_A A' iff f is an isomorphism after iterated derived a_i-adic completion iff A/^L(a_1^n, …, a_r^n) ≅ A'/^L(a_1^n, …, a_r^n) for all n; the condition depends only on I.

items.name: Excision for flat cohomology
items.statement: For a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G, a map A → A' of animated R-algebras and a finitely generated I ⊂ π_0(A) with π_0(A)/I ≅ (π_0(A)/I) ⊗^L_A A', RΓ_I(A, G) ≅ RΓ_I(A', G).
items.locator: Theorem 5.4.4, p. 67; announced as Theorem 1.2.1, p. 6
items.note: Vastly extends Demarche–Harari Lemma 2.6 and Mazur Lemma 5.1.

items.name: Flat cohomology with supports sees only the completion
items.statement: For a Noetherian local (R, 𝔪) and a commutative, finite, flat R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) ≅ H^i_𝔪(R̂, G) for all i; so the main theorem reduces to 𝔪-adically complete R.

items.name: fpqc hyperdescent for flat cohomology
items.statement: For a ring R and a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G, A ↦ RΓ_fppf(A, G) satisfies fpqc hyperdescent on animated R-algebras; for perfect A any faithfully flat A → A' is of universal descent for RΓ_fppf(−, G).
items.locator: Theorem 5.5.2, p. 69; announced as Theorem 1.2.2, p. 6
items.note: Uses the pro-fppf refinement (Lemma 4.1.6), Liu–Zheng Lemma 3.1.2(3) for refinements, and Theorem 4.1.8 for perfect rings.

items.name: p-completely faithfully flat descent
items.statement: For G of p-power order over R and closed Z ⊂ Spec(R/pR), A ↦ RΓ(A^h_{(p)}, G) and A ↦ RΓ_Z(A, G) satisfy hyperdescent for cosimplicial animated R-algebras A → A^• with A/^L p → A^•/^L p an fpqc hypercover.

items.name: Derived I-adic completeness of animated rings
items.statement: An animated ring A is derived I-adically complete for I ⊂ π_0(A) if A ≅ R lim_n A/^L a^n for every a ∈ I; equivalently each π_i(A) is derived a-adically complete for a in a generating set (Bhatt–Scholze 2015, 3.4.4, 3.4.12), and for I = (a_1, …, a_r), A ≅ R lim_n A/^L(a_1^n, …, a_r^n). Classical I-adic completeness of all π_i(A) implies it.
items.note: DD.1 plans derived I-completeness, its Koszul model and the comparison with R lim of derived Koszul quotients.

items.name: Derived complete animated rings are Henselian
items.statement: If A is derived I-adically complete, π_0(A) is I-Henselian.
items.note: Library: Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean:94 (Henselian pairs).

items.name: H^1 of smooth affine groups is invariant under Henselian pairs (Bouthier–Česnavičius)
items.statement: For a Henselian pair (R, I) and a smooth affine R-group Q, H^1(R, Q) ≅ H^1(R/I, Q) and ker(H^2(R, Q) → H^2(R/I, Q)) is trivial; for commutative finite locally free G, H^2(R, G) → H^2(R/I, G) is injective (Bouthier–Česnavičius, Theorem 2.1.6).
items.locator: Section 5.6, p. 71; proof of Lemma 5.6.3, p. 72; proof of Corollary 5.6.9, p. 76

items.name: H^2 of finite flat groups is invariant under Henselian pairs
items.statement: For a Henselian pair (R, I) and a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G, H^2(R, G) ≅ H^2(R/I, G).

items.name: Continuity when high-degree cohomology vanishes
items.statement: If A is derived a-adically complete and H^i(A, G) = H^i(A/^L a, G) = 0 for i ≥ 3 (equivalently for π_0), then RΓ(A, G) ≅ R lim_n RΓ(A/^L a^n, G); for a-adically complete A, H^1 fits in 0 → lim^1 G(A/a^n) → H^1(A, G) → lim H^1(A/a^n, G) → 0.

items.name: a-completely faithfully flat hyperdescent
items.statement: For G commutative, finite, locally free over R and cosimplicial animated A-algebras A → A^• all derived a-adically complete with A → A^• a faithfully flat hypercover modulo a, RΓ(A, G) ≅ R lim_Δ RΓ(A^•, G).

items.name: The continuity formula for flat cohomology
items.statement: For a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G, an animated R-algebra A and I = (a_1, …, a_r) ⊂ π_0(A) with A derived I-adically complete, RΓ(A, G) ≅ R lim_n RΓ(A/^L(a_1^n, …, a_r^n), G).
items.locator: Theorem 5.6.6, p. 75; announced as Theorem 1.2.4, p. 6
items.note: Suggested by Mathew in analogy with Dundas–Morrow, Theorem 1.5.

items.name: Flat cohomology of complete rings
items.statement: For R derived complete for I = (a_1, …, a_r) and G commutative, finite, locally free: H^i(R, G) → H^i(R/I, G) is surjective for i ≥ 1 and bijective for i ≥ 2, and 0 → lim^1 H^0(R/^L(a_1^n, …, a_r^n), G) → H^1(R, G) → lim H^1(R/I^n, G) → 0 is exact, with lim^1 G(R/I^n) as the first term when R is I-adically complete. The Henselian analogue fails: H^1(𝔽_p{t}, μ_p) is countable while H^1(𝔽_p⟦t⟧, μ_p) is not (Remark 5.6.8).

items.name: Invariance of flat cohomology under Henselian pairs
items.statement: For a Henselian pair (R, I) and a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G, H^i(R, G) → H^i(R/I, G) is surjective for i ≥ 1 and bijective for i ≥ 2.
items.note: The case G = μ_n is an unpublished result of Gabber; the proof passes to completions by Bouthier–Česnavičius Lemma 2.1.3, which rests on Popescu's theorem.

items.name: Algebraization of flat cohomology
items.statement: Let B be a topological ring with an open nonunital subring B' that is Henselian and has a neighbourhood base of 0 consisting of ideals of B', and let B̂ be its completion. For commutative, finite, locally free G, H^i(B, G) ≅ H^i(B̂, G) for i ≥ 2 (for instance B = R{t}[1/t] with B̂ = R((t))). Likewise, for A → A' with π_0(A) I-Henselian, π_0(A') I-Henselian and π_0(A)/I ≅ (π_0(A)/I) ⊗^L_A A', H^i(U_A, G) ≅ H^i(U_{A'}, G) for i ≥ 2, and for Noetherian R → R' with R/I^n ≅ R'/I^nR', H^i(U, G) ≅ H^i(U_{R'}, G) for i ≥ 2 and opens U ⊇ Spec(R) ∖ V(I).
items.note: Uses the axiomatic criterion of Bouthier–Česnavičius, Theorem 2.1.15; the G = μ_n case of Corollary 5.6.13 was announced by Gabber (1993, Theorem 2.8(ii)).

items.name: Complete flat modules over perfectoid rings are discrete
items.statement: For a perfectoid A that is derived I-adically complete for finitely generated I = (a_1, …, a_r) and a derived I-adically complete animated A-module M, if each M/^L(a_1^n, …, a_r^n) is flat over A/^L(a_1^n, …, a_r^n), then M is 0-truncated.
items.note: Uses Yekutieli, Flatness and completion revisited, Theorems 2.8, 4.3 and 6.9.

items.name: Adically faithfully flat descent for cohomology with supports
items.statement: For G commutative, finite, locally free over R, an animated R-algebra A, I = (a_1, …, a_r) ⊂ π_0(A) and cosimplicial A → A^• with A/^L(a_1, …, a_r) → A^•/^L(a_1, …, a_r) a faithfully flat hypercover, RΓ_I(A, G) ≅ R lim_Δ RΓ_I(A^•, G); if A and the A^i are derived I-adically complete, then also RΓ(A, G) and RΓ(U_A, G) satisfy this descent.

items.name: The Brauer group of a scheme
items.statement: For a scheme X, Br(X) = ∪_{n>0} im(H^1(X, PGL_n) → H^2(X, 𝔾_m)_tors), the classes of Azumaya algebras.
items.note: Library: Mathlib/Algebra/Azumaya/Defs.lean:60 (Azumaya algebras) and Mathlib/Algebra/BrauerGroup/Defs.lean:99 (the Brauer group of a field).

items.name: Gabber's theorem: Br = H^2(𝔾_m)_tors with an ample line bundle
items.statement: If a scheme X has an ample line bundle (for instance X quasi-affine), Br(X) ≅ H^2(X, 𝔾_m)_tors (Gabber, de Jong); for affine X every torsion class of H^2(X, 𝔾_m) comes from some H^1(X, PGL_n) (Gabber 1981, II Theorem 1).
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.5, p. 90; proof, p. 90; proof of Lemma 5.6.3, p. 72
items.note: Cited from de Jong, A result of Gabber (2002), Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov §4.2, and Gabber, Some theorems on Azumaya algebras.

items.name: p-complete arc hyperdescent for flat cohomology of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For a prime p, a perfectoid ring A, a commutative, finite, locally free A-group G and a closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA), A' ↦ RΓ(A', G) and A' ↦ RΓ_Z(A', G) satisfy hyperdescent for p-complete arc hypercovers whose terms are perfectoid A-algebras.
items.locator: Theorem 5.5.1, p. 68; announced (for G of p-power order) as Theorem 1.2.3, p. 6
items.note: Reduce to Z = Spec(A/p) by excision and arc descent for RΓ(A'[1/p], G); for G of p-power order use the p-adic continuity formula and the deformation triangle to reach A'/^L p, pass to colim A'/^L π^{1/p^n} ≅ (A'/p)^red, and conclude by Theorem 4.1.8 and Proposition 4.2.7.

items.name: The key formula
items.statement: For a prime p, a perfectoid ring A, a commutative, finite, locally free A-group G of p-power order and a closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA), there is an identification RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1}, functorial in A, G and Z (with a fixed ξ defining V over perfectoid A-algebras).
items.locator: Theorem 6.1.1, p. 82; equation (6.1.1.1); announced as (1.1.6), p. 4
items.note: Both sides satisfy p-complete arc hyperdescent (Theorem 5.5.1, Proposition 4.2.7), products of rank ≤ 1 valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields form a base (Lemma 2.2.3), and on them both sides are concentrated in degree 0 and identified by Proposition 4.2.10.

items.name: Purity for flat cohomology of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For a prime p, a perfectoid ring A, a commutative, finite, locally free A-group G of p-power order, a closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA) and an A-regular sequence a_1, …, a_d vanishing on Z, H^i_Z(A, G) = 0 for i < d.
items.locator: Theorem 6.1.2, p. 82; announced as Theorem 1.1.5, p. 4
items.note: By the key formula it suffices that H^i_Z(A_inf(A), A_inf(A)) = 0 for i < d + 1, which follows from the regular sequence ξ, a_1, …, a_d: depth_Z(A) ≥ d implies depth_Z(A_inf(A)) ≥ d + 1.

items.name: Completions of flat modules are flat (Yekutieli)
items.statement: For an ideal I in a Noetherian ring R, every I-adically complete R-module M that is I-completely flat (M ⊗^L R/I concentrated in degree 0 and R/I-flat) is flat; in particular the I-adic completion of a flat R-module is flat.
items.note: Cited from Yekutieli, Flatness and completion revisited, Theorems 1.3 and 1.5; DD.1 plans the bounded-torsion criteria for complete flatness and complete faithfully flat descent.

items.name: Regular sequences survive adic completion
items.statement: For a ∈ A with a-adic completion Â, an A-regular sequence a_1, …, a_n such that each A/(a_1, …, a_i) has bounded a^∞-torsion is Â-regular, and Â/(a_1, …, a_n) ≅ (A/(a_1, …, a_n))^.

items.name: Purity for flat cohomology of complete intersections
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) that is a complete intersection and a commutative, finite, flat R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < dim(R).
items.locator: Theorem 6.2.3, p. 83; announced as Theorem 1.1.1, p. 3
items.note: Reduce to G of p-power order with p = char(R/𝔪) (Theorem 3.2.4 otherwise) and complete R = R̃/(f_1, …, f_n); pass to towers (Lemmas 3.1.1, 4.1.12) and a p-torsion free perfectoid A p-completely faithfully flat over R̃; use the André lemma (Theorem 2.3.4) to adjoin f_i^{1/p^∞}, Lemma 4.1.11 to kill them, and Theorem 6.1.2 on the perfectoid quotient.

items.name: The étale depth is at least the virtual dimension
items.statement: For a Noetherian local (R, 𝔪) and a commutative, finite, étale R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < vdim(R).
items.locator: Theorem 6.2.4, p. 84; announced as Theorem 1.3.1, p. 8
items.note: The reduction of Theorem 3.2.4 leaves G = ℤ/p with p = char(R/𝔪) on a hypersurface, a complete intersection to which Theorem 6.2.3 applies; Remark 6.2.5 records the simplifications available for ℤ/p.

items.name: The complete intersection hypothesis cannot be relaxed to the virtual dimension
items.statement: For R = 𝔽_p⟦x, y, z, t⟧/(x², y², xz − yt), the nonzero element xy dies on U_R = Spec(R) ∖ {𝔪}, so it gives a nonzero class in H^0_𝔪(R, α_p) although vdim(R) = 1.

items.name: Purity for flat cohomology of regular local rings in degree dim(R)
items.statement: For a regular local ring (R, 𝔪) that is not a field and a commutative, finite, flat R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i ≤ dim(R).
items.locator: Theorem 6.2.7, p. 85; announced as the second case of Theorem 1.1.1, p. 3
items.note: After reducing to G = H[p] for a p-divisible group H (Berthelot–Breen–Messing 3.1.1) over R_∞ = W(k)⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f), the key formula turns the claim into the absence of V-fixed points on H^d_Z(R̂_∞^♭, 𝕄(G)), where V is contracting on the monomials (x^♭)^a with a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{<0}^d.

items.name: Global purity for flat cohomology
items.statement: Let X be a scheme, G a commutative, finite, locally free X-group, d an integer and Z ⊂ X a closed subset with X ∖ Z ↪ X quasi-compact such that each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, is either a complete intersection of dimension ≥ d or regular of dimension ≥ max(d − 1, 1). Then H^i(X, G) → H^i(X ∖ Z, G) is injective for i < d and bijective for i < d − 1.
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed version allows regular local rings of dimension d − 1 = 0, where the statement fails (sourceIssues E1). The proof reduces by Lemma 7.1.1 to strictly Henselian X and shrinks Z by Noetherian induction with a Mayer–Vietoris sequence, ending with Theorems 6.2.3 and 6.2.7.

items.name: Auslander's freeness criterion over regular local rings
items.statement: For a regular local ring R and a finitely generated R-module M, if Hom_R(M, M) ≅ M^{⊕r} as R-modules (with M reflexive), then M is free (Auslander, On the purity of the branch locus, Theorem 1.3).

items.name: Purity for torsors and gerbes under finite locally free groups (Moret-Bailly)
items.statement: Let X be a scheme, G a finite, locally free X-group and Z ⊂ X closed with X ∖ Z ↪ X quasi-compact and each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, regular of dimension ≥ 2. Pullback is an equivalence from G-torsors to G_{X∖Z}-torsors, and for every G-gerbe 𝒢, 𝒢(X) ≅ 𝒢(X ∖ Z); hence ker(H^2(X, G) → H^2(X ∖ Z, G)) is trivial.
items.note: A mild generalization of Moret-Bailly, C. R. Acad. Sci. 300 (1985), lemme 2, following Marrama's thesis; the authors expect the complete intersection analogue (dimension ≥ 3) but Auslander's criterion needs regularity.

items.name: Parafactorial and geometrically parafactorial local rings
items.statement: A local ring (R, 𝔪) is parafactorial if pullback is an equivalence from line bundles on Spec(R) to line bundles on Spec(R) ∖ {𝔪}; it is geometrically parafactorial if its strict Henselization is. Noetherian local geometrically factorial rings of dimension ≥ 2 are geometrically parafactorial (EGA IV 21.13.9(ii)), parafactorial rings have depth ≥ 2 (EGA IV 21.13.8), and local rings of dimension ≥ 2 with factorial strict Henselizations have torsion H^{≥2}(𝔾_m) (Grothendieck, Le groupe de Brauer II–III).
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.8, p. 91; footnote to part (a), p. 91; Theorem 7.2.9, p. 92
items.note: Library: Mathlib/RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean:429 (the Picard group of a ring).

items.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz for local complete intersections
items.statement: A Noetherian local complete intersection (R, 𝔪) of dimension ≥ 4 is parafactorial: Pic(U_R) = 0 for U_R = Spec(R) ∖ {𝔪} (SGA 2 XI Théorème 3.13(ii)); a global complete intersection X ⊂ ℙ^n_k of dimension ≥ 3 has Pic(X) = ℤ·[𝒪(1)] (SGA 2 XII Corollaire 3.7).
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.1, p. 88; proof, p. 88; Corollary 7.2.3, p. 89

items.name: Torsion in the local Picard group of a complete intersection (Gabber's Conjecture 3)
items.statement: For a Noetherian local complete intersection (R, 𝔪) of dimension ≥ 3, Pic(U_R)_tors = 0 for U_R = Spec(R) ∖ {𝔪}; if R has dimension ≥ 4 or is regular, Pic(U_R) = 0.
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.1, p. 88; announced as Theorem 1.1.3(a), p. 3
items.note: From H^1(R, μ_n) ≅ H^1(U_R, μ_n) (Theorem 6.2.3). Earlier cases: hypersurfaces (Dao), 𝔽_p-algebras (Gabber; Dao–Li–Miller) and torsion prime to the residue characteristic (Robbiano; SGA 2 X 3.4).

items.name: Cohen–Macaulay rings do not satisfy purity
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and R = ℂ⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧^{ℤ/2} with x_i ↦ −x_i, R is a Cohen–Macaulay normal local domain, ℂ⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ is a nontrivial ℤ/2-torsor over U_R, and it gives a nonzero element of Pic(U_R)[2]; so Theorem 7.2.1 and the main theorem fail for Cohen–Macaulay rings.
items.note: The printed remark says n ≥ 2, which already gives the nonzero element of Pic(U_R)[2]; the failure of Theorem 7.2.1 needs dim(R) = n ≥ 3.

items.name: Picard groups of global complete intersections
items.statement: For a field k and a global complete intersection X ⊂ ℙ^n_k of dimension ≥ 2, (Pic(X)/ℤ·[𝒪(1)])_tors = 0; if dim(X) ≥ 3, Pic(X) is free on [𝒪(1)]. The torsion cannot be dropped (the quadric surface has Pic ≅ ℤ²) nor the dimension lowered (an elliptic curve has infinite Pic_tors) (Remark 7.2.4).
items.note: For smooth X due to Deligne, SGA 7 XI 1.8; the proof passes to the local ring of the affine cone as in Česnavičius, Grothendieck–Lefschetz for vector bundles.

items.name: Grothendieck's results on the cohomological Brauer group
items.statement: For a regular local ring of dimension 2, pullback gives equivalences of vector bundles and of Azumaya algebras over R and over U_R, so Br(R) ≅ Br(U_R) (Le groupe de Brauer III, 6.1 b)); for a Noetherian integral scheme whose strict Henselizations are factorial, H^i(X, 𝔾_m) is torsion for i ≥ 2 (Le groupe de Brauer II, 1.4).
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.5, p. 90; proof, p. 90; proof of Theorem 7.2.9, p. 92

items.name: Purity for the Brauer group of local complete intersections (Gabber's Conjecture 2)
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) that is a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 4 or regular of dimension ≥ 2, Br(R) ≅ Br(U_R) for U_R = Spec(R) ∖ {𝔪}.
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.5, p. 90; announced as Theorem 1.1.3(b), p. 3
items.note: Br = H^2(𝔾_m)_tors on quasi-affine schemes and Pic(R) = Pic(U_R) = 0 reduce to H^2(R, μ_n) ≅ H^2(U_R, μ_n) (Theorems 6.2.3, 6.2.7); regular dimension 2 is Grothendieck's. Reproves Česnavičius (Duke 2019) for regular rings without treating dimension 3 separately; Gabber had the cases of 𝔽_p-algebras and dimension ≥ 5.

items.name: The dimension bounds for Brauer purity are sharp
items.statement: For the local ring S at the vertex of the affine cone over a complex elliptic curve and R = S^sh⟦x, y⟧/(xy), a 3-dimensional strictly Henselian complete intersection, Br(R) = 0 but Br(U_R) is infinite; with ℙ^1 × ℙ^1 instead, H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) contains classes not coming from H^2(R, 𝔾_m).
items.note: Uses Boutot, Schéma de Picard local, V 4.9 and IV 5.1.

items.name: Hartogs extension for separated and affine schemes
items.statement: Let X be a scheme and Z ⊂ X closed. (a) If each 𝔪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, contains an 𝒪_{X,z}-regular element, then Y(X) ↪ Y(X ∖ Z) for every separated X-scheme Y. (b) If each contains an 𝒪_{X,z}-regular sequence of length 2, then Y(X) ≅ Y(X ∖ Z) for every X-affine X-scheme Y.
items.note: The Noetherian case of (b) is EGA IV 5.10.5; the general case uses Koszul complexes K(m_1^n, m_2^n).

items.name: Purity for cohomology of groups of multiplicative type in degrees ≤ 2
items.statement: Let X be a scheme, T a finite type X-group of multiplicative type and Z ⊂ X closed with X ∖ Z ↪ X quasi-compact. (a) If each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, is Noetherian and geometrically parafactorial, then H^0(X, T) ≅ H^0(X ∖ Z, T), H^1(X, T) ≅ H^1(X ∖ Z, T) and H^2(X, T) ↪ H^2(X ∖ Z, T).
items.note: The role of geometric parafactoriality for H^2 was noticed by Strano (1979, Teorema 4).

items.name: Purity for the Brauer group of schemes with complete intersection singularities
items.statement: In the setting of 7.2.8, (b) if each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, is a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 3 (resp. ≥ 4) or regular of dimension ≥ 2, then H^1(X, T)_tors ≅ H^1(X ∖ Z, T)_tors (resp. H^2(X, T)_tors ≅ H^2(X ∖ Z, T)_tors), torsion meaning killed by a locally constant function. In particular, for a Noetherian X, H^2(X, 𝔾_m)_tors ≅ H^2(X ∖ Z, 𝔾_m)_tors when each 𝒪_{X,z} is a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 4 or regular of dimension ≥ 2.
items.locator: Theorem 7.2.8, p. 91; part (b); announced as Theorem 1.1.4, p. 4
items.note: Extends Česnavičius's purity for the Brauer group of regular schemes to complete intersection singularities.

items.name: Purity for groups of multiplicative type in higher degrees
items.statement: Let X be a scheme, T a finite type X-group of multiplicative type, d ≥ 3 and Z ⊂ X closed with X ∖ Z ↪ X quasi-compact, each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, either a complete intersection of dimension ≥ d all of whose strict Henselizations are factorial, or regular of dimension ≥ d − 1. Then H^i(X, T) → H^i(X ∖ Z, T) is injective for i < d and bijective for i < d − 1.
