routes.title: Purity for flat cohomology and the conjectures of Gabber
routes.brief:
Plan purity for flat cohomology after Česnavičius–Scholze, Purity for flat cohomology (Ann. of Math. 199 (2024) 51–180). Final theorems, as stated there: Theorem 6.2.3 (= Theorem 1.1.1): for a Noetherian local complete intersection (R, 𝔪) and a commutative, finite, flat R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < dim(R); Theorem 6.2.7: for regular R that is not a field, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i ≤ dim(R); Theorem 6.1.1, the key formula RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1} for perfectoid A and G of p-power order, and Theorem 6.1.2, purity for perfectoid rings (depth_Z(A) ≥ d gives H^i_Z(A, G) = 0 for i < d); Theorem 6.2.4: H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < vdim(R) for finite étale G over any Noetherian local R; Theorem 3.3.1: Zariski–Nagata purity for vdim ≥ 3; and the global consequences — Theorem 7.1.2 (use the corrected hypothesis 'regular of dimension ≥ max(d − 1, 1)', sourceIssues E1), Theorem 7.1.3 (Moret-Bailly purity for torsors and gerbes), Gabber's Conjectures 2 and 3 (Theorems 7.2.5 and 7.2.1), Corollary 7.2.3 and Theorems 7.2.8–7.2.9 on groups of multiplicative type, including purity for the Brauer group of schemes with complete intersection singularities.

Layers, in order. (1) Virtual dimension and étale depth (Section 3.2): vdim, its independence and additivity, and Theorem 3.2.4 by the hypersurface reduction. (2) Zariski–Nagata for vdim ≥ 3 (Section 3.3), with Zariski–Nagata for regular rings (SGA 2 X 3.4). (3) Positive characteristic (Section 4.1 from 4.1.10): α_p and ℤ/p below depth, Lemma 4.1.11 (the only place the complete intersection hypothesis enters), the finite-cover Lemma 4.1.12 and Proposition 4.1.13. (4) Perfectoid analysis (Section 4.2 from 4.2.4): low-degree cohomology, arc descent for Dieudonné-module cohomology, products and the local analysis over products of valuation rings (with Katz's unit-root lemma). (5) Theorem 5.5.1 and the key formula and perfectoid purity (Section 6.1). (6) The main theorems (Section 6.2), with Lemma 6.2.2 and the counterexample of Remark 6.2.6. (7) Global purity, local Picard and Brauer groups (Section 7), with parafactoriality, Grothendieck–Lefschetz (SGA 2 XI 3.13, XII 3.7), Grothendieck's Brauer results, Auslander's criterion and the Hartogs Lemma 7.2.7; the sharpness examples of Remarks 7.2.2, 7.2.4 and 7.2.6 are tests.

Imports: the proposed Part II of SchemeAndStackFoundations from this extraction (flat cohomology of animated rings: the positive-characteristic key formula 4.1.8, excision, p-adic and general continuity, fpqc descent, Bégueri resolution, Brauer groups of schemes); the proposed Part II of PerfectoidQuotients (perfectoid structure, towers, the ind-syntomic André lemma); the proposed Part II of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves (Gabber–Thomason purity and the local Lefschetz lemma); ArcTopologyAndDescent and PrismaticCohomologyPartIIPrismaticDieudonneTheory as proposed by other extractions; PerfectoidQuotients Q0 and Q3, PrismaticCohomology PR.0, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 (Cohen structure, routed here as a source) and R03.3, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1–SF.4, InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0, DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0–DD.1, Tau Ceti's Cartier duality and Mathlib's IsRegularLocalRing, regular sequences, localCohomology and CommRing.Pic. Tests: G = μ_p, ℤ/p, α_p over 𝔽_p⟦x, y⟧, over a mixed-characteristic hypersurface and over W(k)⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧/(p − f); a perfectoid valuation ring and a product of them; the cone over an elliptic curve; ℂ⟦x_1, x_2, x_3⟧^{ℤ/2}. The pending Česnavičius, Purity for the Brauer group extraction should route here too.
routes.reason: The atlas has no flat cohomology beyond SF.2's site, and no Brauer groups of schemes, local Picard groups or SGA 2 purity. EDC.2 excludes absolute purity, and the perfectoid, prismatic and Dieudonné roadmaps compute cohomology rather than purity. The paper's main line (virtual dimension, the key formula, perfectoid purity, purity for complete intersections, Gabber's conjectures, Brauer purity) has no existing direction, so it is a new roadmap. The general tools it builds are routed to their owners (routes 2–6).

routes.title: Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations, Part II: flat cohomology with finite locally free coefficients over animated rings
routes.brief:
Extend Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations), whose SF.2 owns the fppf site and its cohomology, with flat cohomology with commutative, finite, locally free coefficients over animated rings, after Česnavičius–Scholze, Purity for flat cohomology, Sections 4.1 and 5. Final theorems: Theorem 5.2.6 (fppf hyperdescent and Postnikov convergence over animated rings; étale = fppf for smooth groups), Theorem 5.2.8 (the deformation triangle RΓ(A', G) → RΓ(A, G) → RHom(e^*L_{G/R}, M[1])), Theorem 4.1.8 (for perfect 𝔽_p-schemes, Rε_*G → 𝕄(G) → 𝕄(G) with V − 1, so RΓ_Z(S, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(W_n(S), 𝕄(G))^{V=1}), Theorem 5.3.5 (p-adic continuity RΓ(A, G) ≅ R lim RΓ(A/^L p^n, G) for p-Henselian π_0(A)), Corollary 5.3.7 (H^{≥3} = 0, and H^{≥2} = 0 when (π_0 A/p)^red is perfect), Theorem 5.4.4 (excision RΓ_I(A, G) ≅ RΓ_I(A', G) when π_0(A)/I ≅ (π_0(A)/I) ⊗^L_A A'), Corollary 5.4.5, Theorem 5.5.2 (fpqc hyperdescent), Corollary 5.5.3, Theorem 5.6.6 (continuity for derived I-adically complete A), Corollary 5.6.9 (invariance under Henselian pairs in degrees ≥ 2), Corollaries 5.6.10–5.6.13 (algebraization) and Theorem 5.7.2 (adically faithfully flat descent with supports).

Layers: (1) ind-fppf and ind-syntomic maps, the pro-fppf site and its stability under perfection, and the Bégueri resolution; (2) animated deformation theory of group schemes (Proposition 5.1.5, Example 5.1.10, 5.1.11–5.1.14); (3) flatness, étale sites and cohomology over animated rings (Section 5.2); (4) the positive-characteristic key formula (Proposition 4.1.4 to Corollary 4.1.9); (5) p-adic continuity (Section 5.3); (6) excision (Section 5.4); (7) fpqc and p-complete descent (Theorem 5.5.2, Corollary 5.5.3); (8) derived-complete continuity, Henselian pairs and algebraization (Section 5.6); (9) adic descent (Section 5.7); (10) the Brauer group of a scheme and Gabber's theorem Br = H^2(𝔾_m)_tors with an ample line bundle.

Imports: SF.0–SF.4 (parent); EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2 and E5 (animation, presentability, descent); DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0–DD.1 (cotangent complex, square-zero extensions, derived completion); crystalline Dieudonné theory over perfect bases from PrismaticCohomologyPartIIPrismaticDieudonneTheory (Anschütz–Le Bras extraction, with this extraction's additions); arc descent, formal glueing and Gabber's affine proper base change from ArcTopologyAndDescent; PerfectoidQuotients Q0; Tau Ceti's FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDual; Mathlib's HenselianRing, fppfTopology and IsAzumaya. Tests: μ_p, ℤ/p, α_p over 𝔽_p[t], its t-Henselization and 𝔽_p⟦t⟧ (Remark 5.6.8); a non-p-torsion-free ring where A/^L p is not discrete; a perfect ring; a square-zero extension; the Henselian pair (ℤ_(p)^h, p).
routes.reason: Excision, continuity, fpqc descent, invariance under Henselian pairs and the animated deformation triangle are general properties of fppf cohomology, the direction of SF.2 (which owns the fppf site and its cohomology), and the purity roadmap is only one consumer. The Brauer group of a scheme is placed here with them.

routes.title: Perfectoid quotients and their prismatic prerequisites, Part II: structure of integral perfectoid rings and the ind-syntomic André lemma
routes.brief: Extend Perfectoid quotients and their prismatic prerequisites (PerfectoidQuotients), whose Q0 constructs integral perfectoid rings with A_inf and θ and whose Q3 proves André's flatness lemma (Bhatt–Scholze 7.14), with the structure theory of integral perfectoid rings used by Česnavičius–Scholze, Purity for flat cohomology, Sections 2.1 and 2.3. Final theorems: Theorem 2.3.4, the ind-syntomic André lemma (a faithfully flat, ind-syntomic, ϖ-Henselian A-algebra A' with perfectoid completion and a ϖ-divisible ideal I' with A'/I' faithfully flat, in which every monic polynomial has a root with compatible p-power roots modulo I'), Corollary 2.3.7 (semiperfectoid covers of p-Zariski rings), Proposition 2.1.11 (stability under adjoining roots, completed tensor products, quotients by ideals with p-power roots, products and adic completions), the canonical decomposition 2.1.3 and reducedness, Proposition 2.1.4 (fibre products), Corollary 2.1.6, p-integral closedness (2.1.7) and Proposition 2.1.8, the valuation-ring part of Proposition 2.1.9, Proposition 2.1.12, and Lemma 3.1.1 (perfectoid towers over complete regular local rings). Layers: basic identities (2.1.2), decomposition and fibre products, p-integral closure, tilting of valuation rings, stability properties, torsion-free covers, the approximation Lemma 2.3.1 and the nilpotence Lemma 2.3.2, the André lemma, and towers. Imports: Q0 and Q3, PrismaticCohomology PR.0 (perfect prisms and the tilting equivalence), PerfectoidSpaces P1 (Scholze's rank-one tilting, Theorem 3.7), Tau Ceti's adic-spaces roadmap for continuous valuations, the ind-syntomic maps of this extraction's SchemeAndStackFoundations Part II, and Mathlib's PreTilt and WittVector.fontaineTheta. Tests: O_C, the completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}], a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra, O_C/(p^{1/p^∞}), a product of perfectoid valuation rings, and W(k)⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f) in both the ramified and unramified cases.
routes.reason: Q0 owns integral perfectoid rings and Q3 André's lemma; the decomposition, stability, p-integral closure, approximation and ind-syntomic refinement are general structure results in that direction, not specific to purity.

routes.title: Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves, Part II: absolute cohomological purity and Gabber's local theorems
routes.brief: Extend Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves), whose EDC.2 proves smooth purity and explicitly excludes Gabber's absolute purity for regular schemes, with that theorem and the local results on excellent schemes it needs, following Česnavičius–Scholze, Purity for flat cohomology, Sections 2.2 and 3.1–3.2. Final theorems: Theorem 3.1.3 (absolute cohomological purity: for a regular local (R, 𝔪) and a finite étale commutative G of order invertible in R, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < 2 dim(R)), with the reduction of full purity (the cycle class isomorphism in degree 2 dim(R)) to positive characteristic of Remark 3.1.4; Theorem 2.2.7 (algebraic tilting of idempotents and étale cohomology: RΓ_ét(U, G) ≅ RΓ_ét(U^♭, G) and RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(A^♭, G)); and Lemma 3.2.3 (the local Lefschetz hyperplane theorem). Also plan the inputs from Illusie–Laszlo–Orgogozo, Travaux de Gabber: the affine Lefschetz theorem (XV 1.2.4), dualizing complexes on excellent regular schemes with their normalization (XVI 3.1.1, XVII 0.2) and local duality (SGA 5 I). Follow the perfectoid proof: Artin's case in equal characteristic, finite flat traces (EDC.2), the towers and completed ind-étale perfectoids of this extraction's PerfectoidQuotients Part II, and tilting by arc descent from ArcTopologyAndDescent; Gabber's and Thomason's proofs are alternatives. Imports: EDC.0–EDC.2 (parent), SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2, PerfectoidQuotients Q0 and PrismaticCohomology PR.0. Tests: equal characteristic k⟦x, y⟧; W(k)⟦x⟧ and W(k)⟦x, y⟧/(p − xy) with ℓ ≠ p; and the tilt of W(k)⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − x).
routes.reason: Absolute purity, affine Lefschetz and dualizing complexes on excellent schemes continue EDC's duality and purity theory beyond schemes of finite type over a field; EDC.2 names absolute purity as out of its scope.

routes.title: The arc-topology and descent for étale cohomology
routes.brief: This route adds a consumer to the new roadmap ArcTopologyAndDescent proposed by the Bhatt–Mathew arc-topology extraction (PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21) and followed by the Bhatt–Scholze, Clausen–Mathew–Morrow and Guo–Reinecke extractions; follow that brief. Česnavičius–Scholze need its I-complete version: I-complete arc covers detected on I-adically complete rank ≤ 1 valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields, the examples (faithfully flat maps, maps faithfully flat modulo powers of I, integral surjections), products of such valuation rings as a base with the ultraproduct description of their connected components and the absence of nonsplit étale covers, arc and I-complete arc hyperdescent for étale cohomology of rings, punctured I-completions and I-Henselizations (Bhatt–Mathew 5.4, 6.11, 6.17; Mathew 5.18), formal glueing (6.4), Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change, the Fujiwara–Gabber comparison of Henselian rings with their completions (Bouthier–Česnavičius 2.3.4), the tilting invariance of ϖ-complete arc covers of perfectoid rings, and Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms, Proposition 8.10 (p-complete arc hyperdescent for A, A^♭ and A_inf on perfectoid rings). Import integral perfectoid rings from PerfectoidQuotients Q0 and the tilting equivalence from PrismaticCohomology PR.0. Unit tests: a product of rank-one valuation rings as a p-complete arc cover, a rank-two valuation ring, and descent along O_C → ∏ V_j.
routes.reason: Four extractions already propose this roadmap for the arc-topology and arc descent of étale cohomology; the I-complete variants, the base of products of valuation rings and Bhatt–Scholze 8.10 belong with them rather than in a second arc roadmap.

routes.title: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants, Part II: prismatic Dieudonné theory
routes.brief: This route adds a consumer to the Part II of PrismaticCohomology proposed by the Anschütz–Le Bras extraction (PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23), prismatic Dieudonné theory; follow that brief. Česnavičius–Scholze use the torsion part: the covariant classification of commutative, finite, locally free groups of p-power order over a perfectoid ring A by finitely presented, p-power torsion A_inf(A)-modules of projective dimension ≤ 1 with F and V, FV = Frob(ξ) and VF = ξ (Anschütz–Le Bras 5.4), its exactness and base change, and the modules of μ_{p^n} and ℤ/p^n. Add its crystalline predecessor over perfect 𝔽_p-schemes (Berthelot 1980, Gabber, Lau 2013 Corollary 6.5): the Zariski-glued equivalence G ↦ 𝕄(G) with quasi-coherent W(𝒪_S)-modules, defined through embeddings into p-divisible groups and the covariant Dieudonné crystal of Berthelot–Breen–Messing, its compatibility with base change along perfect schemes, its exactness, and its identification with the prismatic functor for perfect rings (Anschütz–Le Bras 4.44). Unit tests: ℤ/p^n, μ_{p^n} and α_p over a perfect field and over a perfect ring with nontrivial idempotents, and the p-torsion of a p-divisible group.
routes.reason: The Anschütz–Le Bras extraction proposes this Part II for prismatic Dieudonné theory, including the classification over perfectoid rings; the crystalline classification over perfect bases is its perfect-ring case and is added to it rather than planned separately.

R03.1 constructs complete local coefficient categories and presentations of complete local rings as quotients of power series rings; the Cohen structure theorem is the statement those presentations rest on, and this paper uses it in the unramified mixed-characteristic form.
